slot.brief: Two straightforward universal statements with clear overlap; ask which conclusions definitely follow (no 'possibility' cases).

stem:
**Statements:**
All violins are instruments.
All instruments are objects.

**Conclusions:**
I. All violins are objects.
II. All objects are instruments.

verdicts.working: Violins ⊆ instruments ⊆ objects, so I follows. The statements do not imply that all objects are instruments, so II does not follow.

working:
All violins are within instruments, and all instruments are within objects; hence all violins are objects. The reverse inclusion in II is not stated.

Independent check: Violins ⊆ instruments ⊆ objects, so I follows. The statements do not imply that all objects are instruments, so II does not follow.
solution: Since all violins are instruments and all instruments are objects, $$\text{Violins} \subseteq \text{Instruments} \subseteq \text{Objects}.$$ Hence, conclusion I follows. The statements do not imply that all objects are instruments, so conclusion II does not follow.
